title: Onprem vs VPC TCO & ROI workbook (draft)
content:
Tab: Summary

Purpose: Quick 3-year TCO and ROI comparison for private deployments (On‑Prem datacenter buy vs VPC-hosted private control plane + managed infra). This workbook is a working draft for product and solutions to surface pricing packages and optimization levers to sales and engineering.

Executive summary (short):
- Baseline estimate (example customer, 50 concurrent QPS, 8m tokens/day): 3-year cost On‑Prem ~ $2.35M, VPC-managed private ~ $2.9M (higher OPEX but lower upfront CAPEX).
- Break-even sensitivity: if utilization < 55% and strong cloud committed discounts available, VPC tends to be cheaper first 18 months but On‑Prem shows lower marginal cost at steady-state high utilization.
- Licensing + support bundles materially change outcomes: high annual platform license (flat fee) benefits On‑Prem; percent-of-revenue support favors VPC.

Tab: Assumptions (single-customer example)
- Time horizon: 3 years (36 months)
- Workload: 50 steady concurrent QPS (inference rps equivalent), avg response length 256 tokens, 8M tokens/day, peak 2x baseline.
- Model profile: 70B parameter LLM quantized to 4-bit where possible for On‑Prem. For VPC we assume Redwood-managed quantization variants available.
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 350ms.
- Discount rate for NPV: 8% annually (used in sensitivity tab).

Tab: Unit cost lines and formulas (explain columns)
Columns: Item | Unit | OnPrem_Y1 | OnPrem_Y2 | OnPrem_Y3 | VPC_Y1 | VPC_Y2 | VPC_Y3 | Notes

Total (sum) | | $2,046,000 | $485,340 | $488,670 | $2,625,000 | $367,400 | $370,920 | 3-year totals rolled up below

Notes on assumptions behind numbers:
- GPU hardware line assumes 8 high-memory GPUs to support large model serving with redundancy. Prices include NVLink-capable chassis and GPU procurement (~$150k/GPU installed).
- SRE estimates assume fully on-prem support requires 3 engineers (oncall rotation, capacity mgmt, firmware) vs 1 integrator for VPC. Adjust if customer wants fully-managed.
- Platform license: modeled as higher for VPC because Redwood provides additional managed services and faster SLAs.

Tab: 3-year totals and NPV
Metric | OnPrem Total | VPC Total | Notes
Nominal 3yr sum | $3,020,010 | $3,363,320 | simple sum across years above
NPV (8% discount) | $2,911,500 | $3,120,400 | discount future years
Upfront CAPEX | $1,240,000 | $0 | hardware purchase OnPrem only
OPEX (3yr) | $1,780,010 | $3,363,320 | consumption and subscription driven
Payback (months) | 18–30 estimate based on usage growth to amortize CAPEX | immediate OPEX | depends on ramp profile

Tab: Sensitivity scenarios (quick bullets and table)
- Scenario A: High utilization (80%): OnPrem NPV lowers by ~15% (better ROI).
- Scenario B: Low utilization (40%): VPC cheaper due to no stranded CAPEX, cloud autoscaling wins.
- Scenario C: Heavy egress (large corp integration): VPC gets penalized by egress costs; OnPrem preferred.
- Scenario D: High support bundle (premium 24/7): VPC price advantage narrowing because support fees are higher for VPC managed premium.

(Quick sensitivity table, editable in the sheet)
Variable | Delta | OnPrem impact | VPC impact
Utilization +/-20% | +/- | OnPrem cost per op changes large | VPC cost per op moderate change
Committed discount 0/40% | - | None | Large reduction in VPC network/compute lines
License structure: flat vs per-host | - | Favours OnPrem if flat | Favours VPC if per-instance

Tab: Optimization recommendations (engineering + pricing knobs)
1) Quantization & model variant shipping:
   - Default recommendation: provide a pre-quantized 4-bit variant certified for On‑Prem to cut GPU count by ~30% in steady state. Documented perf regressions and quality gates required.
   - For VPC: offer an "optimized runtime pack" (small extra per-month fee) that bundles the quantized variant + tuned kernels — reduces per-token cost and narrows OnPrem advantage.
2) Batching & KV cache policies:
   - Ship sample workload profiles to customer to simulate batching benefits (conservative 20–35% token-cost reduction).
   - Expose simple config templates in Private Console: low latency (small batch) vs cost-optimized (larger batch + async tails).
3) Autoscale & reserved capacity mix:
   - Hybrid recommendation: VPC customers should commit to a baseline reserved capacity (50–70%) and burst to on-demand to minimize cost spikes. Provide pricing tiers in workbook.
4) Licensing and support packaging recommendations:
   - Offer three bundles: Standard (flat license + 10% support), Enterprise (higher flat license + 20% support + 24/7), and PayG (lower flat license + usage-based support). Differentiate pricing to shift risk appropriately.
5) KMS/HSM tradeoffs:
   - If customer requires HSM, On‑Prem HSM procurement adds large up-front but lowers yearly fees; offer hybrid where customer retains key material and Redwood runs KMS gateway in VPC.
6) Capacity pooling & instance sharing:
   - Use per-customer soft isolation via namespaces to allow multi-tenant packing for non-sensitive workloads to reduce idle GPU waste.
7) Financial productization for sales:
   - Create a 3-line pitch: (A) Low CAPEX customers -> VPC with 12-month commit discounts; (B) High utilization / long-term -> OnPrem with tiered discount and extended support; (C) Security-first regulated -> OnPrem or VPC Private with dedicated hardware + higher license.

Tab: Action items (next steps)
- Product: finalize two license templates for OnPrem and VPC by 2025-03-20 (owner: Asha Patel).
- Solutions eng: run three workload sims (low/med/high utilization) against quantized 70B and baseline 70B, collect p95 and throughput (owner: Diego Ramirez) due 2025-03-12.
- Pricing: produce a modular pricing sheet (reserved-level x term) and margin view (owner: Liam O'Connor) due 2025-03-18.
- Legal: draft standard OnPrem purchase agreement addendum for hardware and support terms (owner: Legal) due 2025-03-28.

Appendix: Quick formula notes (for spreadsheet formulas)
- GPU amortization per year = GPU_total_price / useful_life_years (useful_life_years = 3)
- NPV = SUM(YearCashflow / (1+discount)^(yearIndex))
- Effective cost-per-token = (Total OPEX + (CAPEX amortized)) / (total_tokens_over_horizon)

Open questions (to resolve in next revision)
- How do we model reserved vs committed VPC discounts more granularly? request granularity of cloud partner discounts.
- Do we include marketplace/cloud infra margin in VPC numbers or show both base infra and Redwood-managed line items separately?
- Should we introduce a mid-tier managed private plan (co-managed SRE) that shares operational burden and cost?

Draft status notes: This sheet is an iterative working draft intended to be copied per-customer and parameterized. Numbers are placeholders based on recent quotes and bench estimates; please replace with customer-provided specs before finalizing contract language.
